To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CHRoME is a multi-user beamforming system that achieves 2x the throughput of IEEE 802.1ac and is robust to mobility, inter-user interference, and imperfect Channel State Information (CSI); 2) CHRoME uses a custom multi-user probing signal to measure inter-user interference and a fast retransmit scheme that exploits liberated antennas to increase SINR; 3) CHRoME's probing and fast retransmit schemes can be implemented in commodity hardware
CHRoME is an efficient, practical, and effective multi-user beamforming protocol that is resilient to mobility, interference, and channel uncertainty.

CHRoME: 1) increases the resilience of multi-user beamforming systems to inter-stream and intra-stream interference, 2) achieves multi-fold throughput improvements over 802.11 ac, and 3) is robust to imperfect CSI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of resilient multi-user beamforming systems.
the design of resilient multi-stream systems that are robust to mobility and imperfect channel state.

the design and evaluation of a new multi-user beamforming protocol for WLANs that addresses the inherent challenges associated with mobility, inter-stream interferences and imperfect channel state knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CHRoME is a novel, robust, and practical MUBF protocol that achieves significant gains in terms of throughput, fairness, and energy efficiency.
CHRoME is a robust MUBF protocol that achieves multi-fold throughput increases over 802.11a and 802.11n, and is robust to mobility, interference, and CSI imperfections.
CHRoME is an efficient and practical MUBF protocol, and that it can be used to increase the throughput of MUBF WLANs by a factor of up to three.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CHRoME is the first MUBF protocol to address the inherent sensitivity of MUBF WLANs to mobility, interference and imperfect channel state estimation, and is able to achieve multi-fold throughput gains.
we have designed a multi-user beamforming protocol for wireless LANs that addresses the inherent sensitivities of such systems to mobility, interference, and inaccurate channel state information.
CHRoME is the first MUBF system that is resilient to the effects of mobility, interference, and channel estimation errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

MUBF WLANs, while being more sensitive to mobility and inter-stream interference than single-user MIMO systems, can achieve higher throughput and better fairness than single-user MIMOs in the presence of interference.
the design of multi-stream systems must account for the inherent sensitivity to mobility and interference, as well as imperfect CSI, and that this sensitivity is a key design parameter.

the design of MUBF WLANs should not be limited to the design of a single transmission, but rather should consider the full transmission sequence, including retransmissions, and exploit the flexibility offered by multi-user beamforming.
